johnstown-castle: A 19th-century neo-Gothic castle with lakes, gardens and the Irish Agricultural Museum.
irish-national-heritage-park: A 35-acre park recreating 9,000 years of Irish history: Mesolithic huts, a crannóg, a monastery and a Norman ringwork.
coumshingaun-loop: A circular trail around a glacial lake in an amphitheatre of cliffs — one of the most spectacular walks in the south.
ardmore-round-tower: St Declan's monastic site with a 30 m round tower, a carved cathedral and an early oratory.
lismore-castle-gardens: Historic gardens of the castle of the Dukes of Devonshire, with upper and lower gardens above the River Blackwater.
mount-congreve-gardens: One of Europe's largest private gardens, with 70 acres of azaleas, rhododendrons and woodlands planted by Ambrose Congreve.
copper-coast-geopark: A 25 km coastline of cliffs, beaches and 460-million-year-old volcanic geology, a UNESCO heritage site.
waterford-greenway: A 46 km greenway along a former railway, with viaducts, a tunnel and a crossing of the River Suir — the most popular in Ireland.
reginals-tower: A 13th-century Viking tower, Ireland's oldest civic building in continuous use.
waterford-treasures: A group of museums about Viking and medieval Ireland, in the heart of the Viking Triangle.
house-of-waterford-crystal: The Waterford Crystal factory and visitor centre, with a tour of the production floor and a gallery of one-of-a-kind pieces.
woodstock-gardens: Restored Victorian gardens of the Tighe mansion, with an arboretum, an avenue of yews and views over the Nore valley.
jerpoint-park: The lost medieval town of Newtown Jerpoint, with the church of St Nicholas and legends about the saint.
castlecomer-discovery-park: An adventure park in 80 acres of woodland, with treetop walks, zip lines, canoeing and trails.
dunmore-cave: A limestone cave with dramatic formations and a history linked to a 10th-century Viking attack.
smithwicks-experience: A tour of Kilkenny's former brewery, where Smithwick's ale has been brewed since 1710.
rothe-house-garden: A 17th-century Tudor merchant's house, the only one of its kind open to the public in Ireland, with a historically recreated garden.
jerpoint-abbey: A 12th-century Cistercian abbey with exceptional Gothic carvings and sculpted figures on its tombs.
medieval-mile-museum: A museum in St Mary's Church about medieval Kilkenny, with a crypt and merchants' tombstones.
kilkenny-castle: A Norman castle of 1195, seat of the Dukes of Ormonde for six centuries, with Victorian gardens.
clare-island: Grace O'Malley's pirate island at the mouth of Clew Bay, with a walled abbey, a lighthouse and coastal trails.
wild-nephin-ballycroy-national-park: A national park of wild blanket bogs and the Nephin mountains, with a visitor centre and dark skies.
great-western-greenway: A 42 km greenway along a former railway, from Westport to Achill — one of Ireland's most beautiful cycle rides.
ceide-fields: A 5,500-year-old Neolithic field system, the most extensive in the world, beneath the blanket bog of north Mayo.
downpatrick-head: A headland with the Dún Briste sea stack ("broken track"), an old church and St Patrick's well above the Atlantic.
